movesets.name: Dancing Bear
movesets.description:
• After boosting its power through Swords Dance, Urshifu-S can leverage its complementary set of STAB moves to smash through the opposing team.

  • Close Combat versus Drain Punch: Close Combat offers Urshifu-S the maximum sweeping power. However, if using Focus Sash or a defensive Tera type, Drain Punch is handy for restoring enough health after a boost to prevent priority attacks from easily knocking Urshifu-S out.

Items

  • Focus Sash: Focus Sash can help Urshifu-S more reliably get off a Swords Dance boost. It can survive hits from Fairy-types like Flutter Mane as well as powerful special attackers like Iron Bundle. With an Adamant nature, Urshifu-S can reliably beat offensive Tera Fairy Flutter Mane with Wicked Blow + Sucker Punch, provided Focus Sash is still intact.

  • Black Glasses versus Punching Glove: Both items boost the power of Urshifu-S's signature move, Wicked Blow. Black Glasses gives a slightly stronger boost, while Punching Glove helps to protect Urshifu-S from contact effects like Rocky Helmet and Zapdos's Static. Urshifu-S is much less vulnerable to these effects compared to Urshifu-R due to lack of a multi-hit move. Finally, despite the name, Punching Glove does not boost the power of Sucker Punch, while Black Glasses does.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Medium: Typically, Urshifu-S will utilize Terastallization offensively to bolster the power of its Dark-type moves, but this set can benefit more from a defensive Tera type in order to stay on the field longer and make use of its ability to switch moves, which the Choice-locked attacker set cannot.

  • Dark: Tera Dark strengthens Wicked Blow and allows Urshifu-S to power its way through opposing walls. After a Swords Dance boost, Tera Dark-boosted Wicked Blow is a guaranteed OHKO on physically defensive Zapdos, while Close Combat has a high chance to OHKO Ting-Lu.

  • Poison: This Tera type allows Urshifu-S to survive common Fairy-type and Fighting-type attacks that would otherwise threaten to KO Urshifu-S.

  • Ghost: For Focus Sash sets, Tera Ghost blocks Normal-type priority from the likes of Dragonite, Ogerpon formes, or Entei from picking Urshifu-S off.

movesets.name: One Punch!
movesets.description:
• Urshifu-S can punch holes in the opposing team with its strong combination of STAB moves. Additionally, Urshifu-S can benefit from team preview against opponents who mistakenly assume it to be Urshifu-R.

  • U-turn: This move allows Urshifu-S to pivot out of bad matchups and scout out potential Tera types.

  • Iron Head: Iron Head can cover opposing Fairy-types such as Flutter Mane and Mimikyu, which threaten Urshifu-S.

  • Poison Jab: Poison Jab is Urshifu-S's strongest option against Primarina and the rare Azumarill.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Medium: Generally, Urshifu-S will utilize Terastallization offensively in order to extend the reach of its signature move Wicked Blow.

  • Dark: Tera Dark allows Urshifu-S to supercharge its Wicked Blow and muscle its way past various physically defensive foes. Notably, it gives Choice Band Urshifu-S a high chance to 2HKO Dondozo through Leftovers recovery, giving Urshifu-S an advantage against many stall teams.

  • Poison: This is a defensive Tera type that removes Fairy-type and Fighting-type weaknesses, and also absorbs Toxic Spikes.

  • Steel: This Tera type allows Urshifu-S to resist Fairy-type attacks and additionally boosts the power of Iron Head.

strategies.overview:
• Urshifu-S is capable of dealing massive damage with its signature move Wicked Blow and high base Attack, as well as its amazing ability in Unseen Fist, which allows it to bypass Protect and apply constant pressure.

  • Tornadus is a great partner for Urshifu-S, as it provides speed control with Tailwind and can launch powerful Bleakwind Storms into Fighting-types like Urshifu-R that resist Wicked Blow. Many of Urshifu-S's threats, such as Chien-Pao, Flutter Mane, and Urshifu-R naturally outspeed it, so strong speed control is vital. Ogerpon-W can Terastallize to better handle a lot of threats to Urshifu-S such as Chien-Pao, Flutter Mane. and Landorus, and support it with Follow Me. Rillaboom hits most Dark-resistant foes such as Iron Hands and Urshifu-R for high damage, and can support it with Fake Out and priority Grass Glide, which combined with a Sucker Punch from Urshifu-S can OHKO Flutter Mane. In return, Urshifu-S handles Rillaboom's weaknesses, hitting the plethora of Steel- and Dark-types that resist its Grass-type STAB moves such as Kingambit, Incineroar, and Gholdengo.

  • Urshifu-S struggles to break through teams with strong Dark-resistant Pokemon or generally bulky supports like Urshifu-R, Iron Hands, and Tera Fairy Flutter Mane as well as redirection from Amoonguss and Fake Out from Incineroar. Due to its poor defensive typing, middling Speed and lack of coverage, it faces issues against faster teams and its many checks.

movesets.name: Focus Sash
movesets.description:
• Close Combat hits common Dark-resistant Pokemon such as Incineroar and Kingambit. Sucker Punch provides priority and makes up for Urshifu-S's average Speed tier.

  • Urshifu-S uses Tera Dark to fire off strong Wicked Blows or Tera Stellar to boost the damage output of its STAB moves. Tera-boosted Close Combat OHKOes common Incineroar at -1 Attack, and both Tera types will allow Urshifu-S to OHKO Flutter Mane, provided its boost is still intact for Dark-type moves.

  • Focus Sash allows Urshifu-S to survive any one attack, making up for its poor defensive typing. In contrast to Choice items, it gives Urshifu-S the freedom to switch moves and use Detect when threatened, which is especially strong against Fake Out leads.

  • The extra EVs in Defense are to maximize Urshifu-S's chance of surviving a use of Surging Strikes from Tera Water Mystic Water Urshifu-R.

movesets.name: Choice Band
movesets.description:
• Choice Band is used to guarantee an OHKO on common targets like Landorus, Ogerpon-H, Flutter Mane, and even Tornadus that are not invested heavily in physical bulk. Even naturally bulky Pokemon such as Dragonite and Walking Wake can be OHKOed or put in the range for minimal damage to KO them.

  • Poison Jab is excellent coverage, hitting the problematic Fairy-types that Urshifu-S normally struggles with. After Terastallization, you can guarantee an OHKO on almost all Rillaboom, Terastallized Flutter mane, and even bulkier pokemon like Tera Fairy Indeedee-F. U-turn is also a viable move as a pivot option.

  • The Attack investment and Adamant nature are necessary to get the KOs mentioned earlier, such as the OHKO on Landorus and Tornadus. The Defense investment allows Urshifu-S to survive the combination of Tera Normal Choice Band Dragonite's Extreme Speed and Sucker Punch from Adamant Chien-Pao. The Special Defense EVs allow Urshifu-S to take a variety of strong attacks such as Earth Power from Landorus and Bleakwind Storm from Tornadus. The remaining EVs are placed in Speed.

  • Tera Poison is chosen to resist the Fighting- and Fairy-type moves that would otherwise hit Urshifu-S super effectively. Urshifu-S is naturally immune to Psychic and has Dark-type moves to cover for the weakness, and it also naturally threatens Psychic-types like Farigiraf. Tera Dark is also an option, as the extra damage combined with Choice Band is absurd and, combined with good Tailwind support and redirection, is a good choice. However, it requires more careful positioning around threats, as Urshifu-S won't be able to Terastallize out of it's Fairy- and Fighting-type weaknesses.

movesets.name: Offensive Sweeper
movesets.description:
Urshifu-S is used as a generally strong attacker, its Wicked Blow deals massive damage to much of the metagame and ignores Attack drops and Protect, minimizing counterplay. It is a versatile pick on many compositions, as its kit does not need much support and is mainly used to enhance a team's offensive pressure with strong attacks. With Tera Dark, Urshifu-S is capable of OHKOing Pokemon such as both Calyrex formes and Flutter Mane as well as bringing most other targets down to low HP, such as Miraidon and Tornadus. Focus Sash helps Urshifu-S remedy its poor defensive typing, while Sucker Punch is able to somewhat bypass Urshifu-S's middling Speed tier.

Urshifu-S functions well on many teams, but those with strong speed control are where Urshifu-S shines, particularly Trick Room compositions with Calyrex-I, which appreciate the immediate pressure. Trick Room lets Urshifu-S outspeed threats such as Flutter Mane and Zamazenta-C. Additionally, Unseen Fist ignoring Protect means that it is more risky for foes to attempt to stall out Trick Room turns. Urshifu-S struggles against Pokemon that resist Dark, such as opposing Incineroar and Urshifu, as they nullify Urshifu-S's main benefit in dealing big damage with Wicked Blow. While Close Combat is strong, it's less consistent because it doesnt bypass Intimidate and drops Urshifu-S's defenses. Additionally, many of these threats also outspeed and Urshifu-S for super effective damage, such as the Zamazenta-C and Urshifu-R. However, Pokemon like Amoonguss and Incineroar are able to somewhat make up for these weaknesses. Amoonguss provides redirection, resists Fairy and Fighting, and threatens foes with Spore, while Incineroar offers general utility and Fake Out, which foes can't block with Protect at risk of a attack from Urshifu-S. Tera Fairy is also a popular Tera type, used by foes like Raging Bolt and Calyrex-S, which are problematic for Urshifu-S as it cannot break through Tera Fairy users because they resist its STAB combination

movesets.name: Glass Cannon
movesets.description:
Set Details

  • Urshifu-S utilizes its STAB attacks to threaten Restricted Pokemon like Calyrex-S, Calyrex-I, and Terapagos alongside other metagame staples like Chien-Pao, Ursaluna, and Chi-Yu.
  • Focus Sash allows Urshifu-S to take two attacks before it is KOed to maximize its on-field presence. Covert Cloak provides Urshifu-S with a strong matchup against Calyrex-S and Terapagos team compositions featuring dual Fake Out cores.
  • Covert Cloak sets use an EV spread of 132 HP / 236 Atk / 4 Def / 76 SpD / 60 Spe with and Adamant nature. This spread is designed to let Urshifu-S survive at least two Astral Barrages from Life Orb-boosted Calyrex-S and outrun maximum Speed Incineroar, with the remainder of the EVs invested into Attack and Defense.
  • Tera Stellar guarantees Urshifu-S's Wicked Blow OHKOes Lunala through Shadow Shield.

Teambuilding

  • Urshifu-S struggles to sufficiently damage Tera Fairy foes such as Miraidon, Lunala, and Raging Bolt, as well as being threatened by Fairy-type attacks like Dazzling Gleam from Miraidon, Moonblast from Lunala and Flutter Mane, and Play Rough from Zacian-C.
  • Fighting-type attacks are problematic for Urshifu-S. Koraidon and Zamazenta-C outspeed and easily KO Urshifu-S with Collision Course and Body Press after its Focus Sash has been broken. Meanwhile, Urshifu-R and Iron Hands can survive Urshifu-S's attacks and KO it in return with Close Combat and Drain Punch, respectively.
  • Incineroar is threatening, since Urshifu-S struggles to remove it before its damage output is hindered by Intimidate and Will-O-Wisp.
  • A partner Miraidon threatens opposing Miraidon, Raging Bolt, and Koraidon with Draco Meteor and Dazzling Gleam, as well as dealing good damage with Electro Drift to them and Incineroar after they Terastallize.
  • Calyrex-I survives Electro Drift, Draco Meteor, and Thunderbolt from Miraidon and Raging Bolt and easily KOes them alongside Koraidon with Glacial Lance. Urshifu-S returns the favor by checking Calyrex-I's threats like Lunala and Calyrex-S with Wicked Blow and Sucker Punch.
  • Landorus can easily threaten Miraidon, Raging Bolt, and Incineroar with Earth Power and Sandsear Storm in addition to threatening Tera Fairy users with Sludge Bomb. Meanwhile, Urshifu-S threatens the foes that can attack before Landorus or survive its onslaught like Calyrex-S and Lunala.
  • Amoonguss pairs well with Urshifu-S, comfortably surviving and redirecting Fairy- and Fighting-type attacks for it on top of disrupting foes with Spore.

movesets.name: Choice Band
movesets.description:
Set Details

  • Choice Band Urshifu-S uses Wicked Blow to reliably OHKO foes like Calyrex-I, Lunala, Volcarona, and Farigiraf while maintaining its naturally good matchups against Calyrex-S and Indeedee-F.
  • With Close Combat, Urshifu-S is able to threaten KOs on Incineroar, Ursaluna, and even Defense Protosynthesis-boosted Brute Bonnet.
  • U-turn allows Urshifu-S to pivot out in situations that may not be favorable for it while doing significant damage to Brute Bonnet and Indeedee-F. Additionally, U-turn can be used to play around defensive Terastallization from Pokemon like Calyrex-I, Lunala, and Farigiraf.
  • While Choice Band does have the obvious downside of locking Urshifu-S into a move, its newfound ability to OHKO Calyrex-I and Lunala with Wicked Blow, alongside its generally higher damage output, allows it to be much more threatening.
  • Urshifu-S should use either a Brave Nature with 252 HP and Attack EVs or an Adamant Nature with 252 Attack and Speed EVs depending on if it is being used on a team that focuses on Trick Room or not. Trick Room teams should run 0 IVs in Speed, while teams not utilizing Trick Room should use 31 IVs in Speed.
  • Tera Grass is the most common Tera type, as it allows Urshifu-S to avoid Rage Powder and Spore from opposing Pokemon like Volcarona and Amoonguss, respectively.

Teambuilding

  • Choice Band Urshifu-S is weak to Fighting-types like Urshifu-R, Iron Hands, and Zamazenta-C, as they can all survive Urshifu's Close Combat and OHKO it back. However, Urshifu-S can OHKO Zamazenta-C with Close Combat if its Dauntless Shield boost is no longer active.
  • Choice Band Urshifu-S is also susceptible to opposing Pokemon's use of Terastallization, as Pokemon like Calyrex-I and Lunala can use a defensive Tera type to survive a hit from Urshifu-S. Lunala is especially scary for Urshifu-S in these scenarios, as it can sometimes run Tera Fairy and Moonblast to survive a hit and OHKO Urshifu-S in return.
  • Choice Band Urshifu-S is strongest on Trick Room teams that feature Restricted Pokemon like Lunala and Calyrex-I, as those teams can use it to threaten OHKOs on Pokemon like Calyrex-I, Calyrex-S, and Lunala. Lunala and Calyrex-I can assist Urshifu-S in return by setting up Trick Room and allowing it to move before Pokemon like Chi-Yu and Zamazenta-C.
  • Another good teammate for Urshifu-S is Indeedee-F, as it appreciates Urshifu-S's ability to threaten Ursaluna before Trick Room goes up. Indeedee-F supports Urshifu-S well by providing Trick Room and redirection, which both allow Urshifu-S to more effectively take KOs.

strategies.overview:
Draft Order: Round 3 onwards

Price Range: 12-13 points

Tera Price Range: 15-16 points

Overview: Urshifu-S is a good sweeper and wallbreaker, especially when made a Tera Captain. It leverages its high Attack stat, powerful STAB moves, good coverage, and various setup options to be difficult to check defensively. While Urshifu-S is held back by its mediocre Speed, bad special bulk, and, most notably, its glaring 4x weakness to Fairy as well as the inability to hit most Fairy-types neutrally with STAB moves, it can mostly circumvent those issues using Terastallization, making it a very threatening Tera Captain; Urshifu-S is perfectly capable of opening up its teammates with its powerful wallbreaking capabilities or potentially straight up running away with the game as a wincon.
strategies.comments:
Common Roles

Setup Sweeper: Urshifu-S can leverage its good matchups against most Pokemon to set up using Swords Dance, Bulk Up, and Trailblaze; these moves further boost its power or circumvent its mediocre Speed and can turn it into a potent wincon.

Wallbreaker: Urshifu-S utilizes its strong STAB moves and decent coverage to weaken or outright KO a large portion of the metagame. Wallbreaker Urshifu-S is usually best supported by other forms of momentum and entry hazards due to its mediocre Speed and special bulk.

Common Moves

Primary STAB moves: Wicked Blow, Sucker Punch, Close Combat, Drain Punch, Low Kick

Setup moves: Swords Dance, Bulk Up, Trailblaze

Utility moves: U-turn, Taunt, Substitute, Brick Break

Coverage: Fire Punch, Ice Punch, Iron Head, Poison Jab, Rock Slide, Stone Edge, Tera Blast, Thunder Punch, Zen Headbutt

Niche Moves

Throat Chop: Throat Chop's sound move-cancelling property allows it to shut down Pokemon that use Fairy-type sound moves to counter Urshifu-S, such as Hyper Voice Sylveon and a myriad of Alluring Voice users.

Common Items

Punching Glove / Protective Pads: Both of these items protect Urshifu-S from contact-based adverse effects, such as Static, Flame Body, and Rocky Helmet. If Urshifu-S plans on mainly using punching moves, Punching Glove's damage boost is very much appreciated; otherwise, Protective Pads would be preferred.

Choice Band: Choice Band allows Urshifu-S to maximize its damage output and wallbreak with increased ease. This is complemented by the fact that few Pokemon in the metagame want to switch into either of its STAB moves or take chip damage from a Choice Band-boosted U-turn, which makes them unable to check Urshifu-S later.

Choice Scarf: Choice Scarf allows Urshifu-S to circumvent its mediocre Speed immediately and become a fast yet still strong wallbreaker. This also allows it to function better as a fast pivot.

Other Damage-boosting Items: Items such as the Life Orb, Black Glasses, and the Black Belt can be used to boost the power of its attacks, allowing it to reach whatever matchup-specific benchmarks are necessary.

Niche Items

Leftovers: Leftovers may see usage on bulkier Urshifu-S sets that use Substitute and Bulk Up to increase its longevity.

Lum Berry: Lum Berry can be used on setup variants to shrug off status, such as paralysis and burn.

Resistance Berries: These Berries, such as the Roseli, Coba, and Chople kinds, allow Urshifu-S to tank a super effective hit in order to revenge kill a foe or set up.

Mental Herb: Mental Herb can be used to prevent disruption caused by a fast Taunt or Encore user when setting up.

Tera

Though it is outclassed by many similarly priced Fighting-type Tera Captains, Urshifu-S is still a great user of Terastallization, as its performance is significantly increased when made a Tera Captain. Its same-type Tera sets, usually seen on wallbreaker sets that use damage-boosting items, allow it to output stupefying levels of damage with Tera Dark Wicked Blow and Tera Fighting Close Combat. More commonly though, Urshifu-S will use Tera types that improve its matchup against Fairy-types, such as Tera Poison and Tera Steel. Other defensive Tera types, such as Water, Fairy, Fire, and Electric, also function very well on its setup sweeper sets, allowing them more setup opportunities as well as giving them additional strong coverage; the last two make Urshifu-S immune to the otherwise debilitating statuses of burn and paralysis, respectively.

Draft Strategy

Urshifu-S can be a potent setup wincon, especially with Terastallization, so it appreciates its teammates dishing out damage before going in for the sweep. It can also cover the wallbreaking role well, forcing large amounts of damage on opposing Pokemon, allowing your late-game cleaners to thrive. With that being said, its aforementioned downsides of a crippling Fairy weakness and mediocre Speed should be covered for by its supporting cast.

Reliable Fairy-type Counters: Urshifu-S greatly appreciates a teammate absorbing Fairy-type attacks aimed at it and either forcing damage on them or threatening them out. It also appreciates Pokemon that heavily dissuade Tera Fairy from being brought in the preparation phase. Pokemon such as Pecharunt, Gholdengo, and Scizor are fantastic partners to Urshifu-S.

Late-game Cleaners: Urshifu-S excels at weakening opposing defensive Pokemon to allow your other Pokemon to clean up games with ease. Notably, Urshifu-S forces a lot of damage on Fairy-types, as they are its best answer. Pokemon usually hindered by Fairy-types such as Kyurem and Latios, as well as other late-game cleaners like Deoxys-S and Dragonite, greatly appreciate the wallbreaking capabilities of Urshifu-S.

Reliable Pivots: Bringing in Urshifu-S safely to set up or launch its powerful attacks is paramount to unlocking its full potential. Reliable pivots such as Cinderace, Landorus-T, and Zapdos can force switches for Urshifu-S to come in and wallbreak.

Entry Hazard Removal: Urshifu-S does not like being forced to run Heavy-Duty Boots. Entry hazard removal from the likes of Terapagos, Iron Treads, and Glimmora allows Urshifu-S to not be chipped as much when it comes onto the field, facilitating both its Choice item and setup sets. In return, Urshifu-S heavily threatens Ghost-types, or Steel-types in Glimmora's case, which may try to spinblock the previously mentioned hazard removers.

Additional Wallbreakers: While this might overlap with Urshifu-S's wallbreaking role, a second wallbreaker can capitalize on Urshifu-S's ability to force switches and pivot in its partner with U-turn. Other wallbreakers are also appreciated if you desire to use Urshifu-S as a setup wincon. Pokemon such as Iron Moth, Iron Crown, and Ogerpon-H have great offensive synergy with Urshifu-S, as they can deal with Fairy-types for it, as well as easily chipping down the opposition.

Checks and Counters

Fairy-types and Tera Fairy Pokemon: Fairy-types are Urshifu-S's Achilles' heel, hitting it for 4x super effective damage while resisting both its STAB moves. Opposing Tera Captains can turn into a Fairy-type, tank a hit from Urshifu-S, and deal damage to or outright KO Urshifu-S with Tera Blast. Common Fairy-types such as Iron Valiant and Enamorus, as well as common Tera Fairy users such as Raging Bolt and Zarude, can easily force out Urshifu-S or use it as setup fodder.

Faster Offensive Pokemon: Due to Urshifu-S's mediocre Speed and middling bulk, faster offensive Pokemon are able to outspeed and threaten it, leaving it unable to reliably hit the field to set up or wallbreak. Those that do not fear its Sucker Punch, such as Iron Valiant, Tornadus-T, and Greninja, are especially effective.

Bulky Physical Walls: While not perfect answers to Urshifu-S, bulky physical walls can tank a STAB move or two while punishing Urshifu-S with chip damage from Rocky Helmet and other adverse contact effects, unless it's holding Punching Glove or Protective Pads, or forcing it to switch out. Such Pokemon include defensive Great Tusk, defensive Garchomp, and Alomomola.

movesets.name: Choice Band (Spe)
movesets.description:
Choice Band Urshifu-S is a potent offensive wallbreaker with an excellent STAB combination against the metagame. With a Speed donation, Urshifu-S is able to threaten out a lot of frail Pokemon that it wouldn't otherwise. Urshifu-S can choose to inherit in the Attack slot, becoming far stronger, but it prefers the Speed slot because it is relatively slow, it already has high Attack, and Attack-inheriting sets are more awkward to fit onto teams. In terms of moves, Wicked Blow and Close Combat are mandatory. U-turn allows Urshifu-S to generate momentum off the many switches it can force. Poison Jab is great at threatening Fairy-types such as physically defensive Clefable and Primarina, while Sucker Punch is a viable alternative to provide speed control in a pinch, and it is preferred when inheriting from gods slower than Eternatus. Tera Dark is preferred to further boost damage on Wicked Blow and Sucker Punch, allowing Urshifu-S to OHKO fully invested Arceus-Ghost. Tera Poison boosts Poison Jab to achieve a 2HKO on Arceus-Fairy and Clefable with base 115 Defense and it is a good defensive Tera for Urshifu-S. Finally, Tera Fighting boosts the damage of Close Combat.

Zacian-C and Eternatus are excellent gods for Urshifu-S to inherit from. Zacian-C appreciates having a strong offensive wallbreaking partner to overwhelm shared checks such as Clodsire and Skarmory, while Eternatus provides Urshifu-S with a partner that can inherit great Special Attack such as Hisuian Electrode or Landorus, taking advantage of the physically defensive walls Urshifu-S invites in and being a solid progress maker itself. Finally, Arceus is rarely a bad choice of a god, and Urshifu-S fits comfortably onto Arceus structures as a fast wallbreaker. Urshifu-S is quite frail, so it appreciates having solid defensive pieces, like Clodsire and Skarmory, to swap into powerful attacks it cannot take itself—especially Fairy-type attacks. Pokemon like Landorus-T, Pecharunt, and Rotom-W can bring Urshifu-S in safely by forming a VoltTurn core with it so it doesn't have to worry about using its middling bulk to hit the field. These three in particular can take on Zacian-C and Zamazenta, two Pokemon Urshifu-S cannot usually beat. Urshifu-S also likes to be paired with physical attackers that can clean easily, like Sneasler, that benefit greatly from the holes it punches in the opposing team. Finally, entry hazard support from the likes of Hisuian Samurott, Great Tusk, Glimmora, and so forth isn't necessarily mandatory but helps Urshifu-S secure key rolls against walls, such as HP-inheriting Skarmory and physically defensive Primarina.

movesets.name: Custap Berry
movesets.description:
• Custap Berry + Reversal allows Urshifu-S to blow past threats that would otherwise be an issue for it such as Choice Scarf Haxorus and Hisuian Goodra.
  • Wicked Blow hits Cresselia, Pecharunt, Spectrier, Iron Crown, and Metagross.
  • Endure is useful against Choice-locked Pokemon such as opposing Urshifu-S, so that your Urshifu-S can survive on 1 HP, go first the next turn thanks to Custap Berry, and fire back with a 200-Base Power Reversal.
  • Bulk Up is useful to set up against Corviknight, since the Defense boost means Urshifu-S doesn't take as much damage from its Body Press or Brave Bird, and the Attack boost means Wicked Blow does more damage; thanks to Wicked Blow's guaranteed critical hit, it also ignores possible Defense boosts from Iron Defense.
  • Sucker Punch can be used over Bulk Up to win against Choice Scarf Cresselia.
  • The EVs allow Urshifu-S to survive a Close Combat from Choice Scarf Haxorus as well as a Hyper Beam from Choice Specs Spectrier while also having enough Speed for non-Jolly Corviknight. The remaining EVs are put into Attack.
  • Urshifu-S can often struggle against Fairy- and Fighting-type Pokemon such as Sylveon, Iron Valiant, and Urshifu-R, so it appreciates having other Poison- and Fairy-type Pokemon such as Pecharunt and Primarina as teammates.

movesets.name: Assault Vest
movesets.description:
• Assault Vest helps Urshifu-S to survive special hits from Pokemon that it would usually struggle against, like defensive Iron Crown, Porygon-Z, and Volcarona.
  • Wicked Blow damages Iron Crown, Pecharunt, and Cresselia.
  • Close Combat hits non-Chople Berry Hisuian Goodra, both Ursaluna formes, and Porygon-Z.
  • Sucker Punch allows Urshifu-S to attack first against threats like Custap Berry Skeledirge and Spectrier in case it needs to do so.
  • Rock Tomb is utilized to have a mostly guaranteed matchup against Volcarona.
  • Counter helps against physically defensive Pokemon like Donphan; Urshifu-S can't deal much damage to them, but Counter helps it to mitigate this.
  • Its EV spread is designed so that it can always beat Porygon-Z. Its Speed EVs allow it to outspeed maximum Speed Choice Specs Porygon-Z, while its Special Defense investment enables it to survive a Hyper Beam from Modest Choice Scarf variants. The remaining EVs are invested into Attack.
  • Urshifu-S struggles heavily against Fairy-types like Iron Valiant and Sylveon. Due to this, Steel- and Poison-type Pokemon like Scizor and Iron Moth make for good partners.

movesets.name: Chople Berry
movesets.description:
• Urshifu-S can utilize the Chople Berry to maximize its overall bulk, allowing it to survive non-STAB Fighting-type attacks from the likes of Darkrai, Iron Crown, and Ursaluna.
  • Sucker Punch can be utilized to hit Pokemon like Moonblast Cresselia and Custap Berry Hoopa-U.
  • Bulk Up is used as a tool for Pokemon that use Defense-boosting moves like Manaphy, which is usually difficult to break through without the move, while the Defense increase helps Urshifu-S take hits from Ursaluna.
  • The EVs allow Urshifu-S to outspeed Modest Hoopa-U and survive a Choice Specs Focus Blast from it as well as an unboosted Close Combat from Adamant Haxorus.
  • Fighting- and Fairy-type Pokemon like Iron Hands, Sneasler, and Sylveon are still quite rough for Urshifu-S to handle, so Pokemon like Pecharunt and Metagross are quite useful for Urshifu-S to have as teammates.
  • Despite the bulk investment, it's still difficult for Urshifu-S to handle common special attackers like Primarina and Raging Bolt, so specially bulky Pokemon like Florges and Hisuian Goodra can also be nice teammates
